Pool Service and Repair in Phoenix

Weekly cleaning, green pool cleanups, pumps, filters, heaters, tile, leaks and resurfacing. One free call reaches an independent, locally owned pool company that handles the job and prices it itself.

Call (623) 240-0428 Match your problem to a service
  1. Home
  2. Services

Pool service and repair in Phoenix covers two kinds of work: keeping the water clean and balanced every week, and fixing the equipment and surfaces that heat, sun, hard water and dust wear out. Both are handled by the independent pool company you reach through the line, never by the line itself.

Below, every service has its own page explaining what the job involves, what a careful pool technician checks and what to ask before you approve the work. If you are not sure where to start, the table matches common problems to the right page.

How to Choose a Pool Company in Phoenix

What to ask, what a written agreement should cover and how to look a company up on the Arizona ROC search.

Read the guide

Check the license first. Arizona's Registrar of Contractors (ROC) licenses contractors, and its residential classifications include R-6, Swimming Pool Service and Repair. Repairs, equipment replacement and resurfacing generally call for a licensed contractor; whether a cleaning-only service needs a license is not spelled out, so ask the ROC if it matters to you. Ask the company for its ROC license number and look it up on the ROC contractor search (opens in a new tab) before work begins. The line does not check this for you.

Common questions

Can one company handle both weekly cleaning and repairs?

Many pool service companies do both, while some only clean and some only repair or resurface. When you are put through, say everything you need so the company can tell you what it handles. For repair work, ask for its Arizona ROC license number and look it up.

Do you handle public or HOA community pools?

The line is set up for home pools. It does not provide information about public pools or aquatic centers. Commercial and community pools have their own health rules and permits, so ask the company directly whether it takes that kind of work.

Does the line build new pools or install fences?

No. Building new pools, pool fencing, landscaping and pest control are outside what the line connects callers with. For an existing pool's surface, see pool resurfacing.

What if I do not know which service I need?

Call and describe what you see and hear. The assistant passes that along, and the pool company you reach can tell you whether it sounds like cleaning, a filter, the pump or something else, then confirm it in person.

Know what the pool needs? Call the free line

One free call at any hour. Say what the pool is doing and where in the Valley you live, and the line puts you through to an independent, locally owned pool company that sees the pool for itself and sets its own price.
